text.p: In a new slap in the face for President Ernesto Samper, Colombia's National Association of Industrialists (ANDI) said on Friday that he would not be invited to attend its annual meeting next month.
The decision marks the first time in the 52-year history of the powerful industrial group that a sitting president will not be invited to address the annual meeting.
"The (ANDI) board of directors decided, at the request and acting under the mandate of all its members, not to invite the president," a spokesman for ANDI told Reuters.

The ANDI and most other Colombian business associations have called repeatedly for Samper's resignation because of the prolonged political crisis stemming from charges that his 1994 election campaign was partly financed with drug money.
In a survey released earlier this week, it cited the political crisis as one of the leading reasons for a sharp slowdown in industrial production so far this year.
